rows.name: IM-1 Odysseus landing site (Malapert A)
rows.mission_end_source: Intuitive Machines, IM-1 mission update 29 Feb 2024: final transmission as the lunar night began (hour not published; 00:00 UTC used)
rows.mission_note: Odysseus tipped onto its side at touchdown, with its panels tilted away from the low Sun; power ran out about three days before the predicted sunset.

rows.name: IM-2 Athena landing site (Mons Mouton)
rows.mission_end_source: Intuitive Machines / NASA release 7 Mar 2025: mission concluded, batteries depleted (hour not published; 12:00 UTC used)
rows.mission_note: Athena came to rest on its side in a crater with the Sun barely above the hills; its batteries drained within a day, with about twelve days of daylight left.

rows.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 landing site (Mare Crisium)
rows.mission_end_source: Firefly Aerospace, Blue Ghost Mission 1 update 16 Mar 2025: mission concluded at 23:25 UTC, about 5 h after lunar sunset
rows.mission_note: Blue Ghost ran the full lunar day on flat mare. Firefly reported the end about 5 h after the sunset it observed; our flat-horizon sunset falls about 2.5 h after theirs, so the reported end lands 2.4 h after ours.
